# Results — Study 799 (Order-Backlog Drift, RPO)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**growth in a firm's order backlog (ASC-606 Remaining Performance Obligations, RPO) is a
leading fundamental the market underreacts to.** Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `243982cf416a`
(RPO-panel adjusted-close prices).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted close for **38** enterprise/subscription-software US names, 2017-01-03 → 2026-06-30 |
| Signal | EDGAR XBRL `companyconcept` **`RevenueRemainingPerformanceObligation`** (total RPO), + `Revenues` + `Assets`; **842** RPO-YoY-growth events, filings **2018-10-24 → 2026-06-24** (RPO does not exist pre-ASC-606) |
| Ranking | YoY growth in RPO (this quarter's RPO vs the same quarter a year ago), point-in-time at the **filing date** |
| Coverage | one macro regime only: essentially no RPO before 2018; the tercile cross-section is wide only from 2019 (the long-short starts **2019-06** and runs to 2026-06, **85 months**) |
| Statistics | **Newey-West (6-lag)** *t* on the monthly long-short (the decisive HAC statistic); one-sample *t*; Wilson interval on the monthly hit rate; 10,000-draw label-shuffle placebo on the pooled event drift |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag (signal known at month *t*, return of *t+1*); costs one-way × NAV × turnover on **both** legs; **short leg pays 100 bps/yr borrow**; gross and net labelled separately |
| Adjustment | **total-return** (adjusted close) throughout |

Survivorship is named on the Signal axis: the basket is **current survivors** (all still
trading), so acquired/failed software names are absent. For a long-top/short-bottom
*growth* signal the direction is ambiguous (both legs survivors), but on this thin panel it
is a live caveat, not a footnote.

## PRIMARY — calendar-time tercile long-short (the decisive test)

Each month-end, rank the names carrying a fresh RPO-YoY-growth figure into terciles; long
the top, short the bottom, equal-weight; earn the next month's return (one execution lag).

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| months (2019-06 → 2026-06) | 85 |
| avg cross-section / avg one-way turnover | 29.3 names / 0.11 |
| gross long-short | **+100.0 bps/mo** (~+12.0%/yr), Sharpe **0.57**, hit 49/85 = 57.6% (Wilson 95% [47.0%, 67.6%]) |
| long leg / short leg | +220.6 / +120.6 bps/mo (+26.5% / +14.5%/yr) |
| one-sample *t* | +1.51 |
| **Newey-West(6) *t*** | **+1.10** &nbsp;← decisive; **below the desk's t ≥ 2 bar** |
| net @ 10 bps + 100 bps borrow | +89.4 bps/mo (~+10.7%/yr), NW *t* = +0.99, Sharpe 0.51 |
| net @ 20 bps + 100 bps borrow | +87.2 bps/mo (~+10.5%/yr), NW *t* = +0.96, Sharpe 0.49 |

The point estimate is economically large and positively signed — but the
autocorrelation-robust *t* is **+1.10**, so on this tape the return edge **cannot be
distinguished from zero**. Turnover is low (the signal refreshes ~quarterly), so costs
barely dent the point estimate — the edge is undone by *significance*, not by frictions.

## The edge is entirely a 2019-2021 phenomenon (regime concentration)

Splitting the long-short at **2022-01-01** (early-ASC-606 vs the mature panel):

| era | months | LS mean | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2019-06 → 2022-01 (SaaS melt-up) | 31 | **+244.7 bps/mo** | +1.78 |
| 2022-01 → 2026-06 (rate-shock + recovery) | 54 | +16.9 bps/mo | +0.17 |

Whatever edge exists lived in the 2019-2021 subscription-software boom and **evaporates**
in the mature 2022+ panel — a textbook regime-concentration warning against
extrapolating it.

## CROSS-CHECK — pooled event drift (534-style)

Bucket every (ticker, filing) event by RPO growth; top-minus-bottom forward drift, entered
one session after the filing; one-sample *t* + a 10,000-draw label-shuffle placebo.

| horizon | n | top | bottom | long-short | win | *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 21d (≈1m) | 830 | +1.25% | +0.99% | +0.26% | 53% | +0.24 | 0.400 |
| 63d (≈1q) | 805 | +5.28% | +3.86% | +1.41% | 51% | +0.60 | 0.260 |
| 126d (≈2q) | 769 | +8.88% | +5.45% | +3.43% | 50% | +0.98 | 0.144 |

Bucket means at 126d rise monotonically with the signal (**+5.45% / +8.48% / +8.88%**,
low → high), so the *sign* is right at every horizon — but not one horizon clears *t* = 2 or
a placebo *p* < 0.05. The drift grows with horizon (+0.26% → +3.43%), consistent with a
slow underreaction, yet it is never statistically certified on this sample.

## MECHANISM (3rd axis) — does backlog actually lead sales? YES

Pooled OLS of next-quarter revenue YoY growth on this-quarter RPO YoY growth:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| n | 465 |
| slope (next_rev_yoy ~ rpo_yoy) | **+0.313** (iid *t* = **+9.92**, R² = 0.175, corr = +0.42) |
| future-sales-growth spread, top vs bottom RPO tercile | **+39.4% vs +18.6% = +20.8 pp** |

The accounting lead the whole thesis rests on is **real and strong**: names in the top
RPO-growth tercile go on to post ~21 pp faster revenue growth next quarter than the bottom
tercile. Backlog genuinely front-runs the income statement. (The *t* is iid-pooled — events
cluster by calendar quarter — so read it as suggestive of a large effect, not a
calendar-robust HAC statistic.) What the tape does **not** show is the market *mispricing*
that lead in a way we can certify.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic price + RPO-growth panel with a TUNABLE planted forward-return edge; ~7-year
(28-quarter) window matching the real sample; no network.

| world | calendar long-short NW *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.37** (sd 0.85), \|t\| ≥ 2 in **1/20** seeds (≈ the nominal 5% rate) |
| planted edge = 0.15 (seed 799) | LS +198.7 bps/mo, **NW *t* = +3.79** |

The detector does not fire on the null and lights up cleanly on a planted edge — so the
sub-2 real-tape *t* is a genuine reading of a thin, one-regime tape, not a broken pipeline.
*(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The RPO-growth long-short is positively signed on **every** cut (gross
  +100 bps/mo ≈ +12%/yr, Sharpe 0.57, hit 58%; pooled drift monotone and rising to +3.43%
  at 126d) and the *mechanism* is unambiguous (RPO growth → next-quarter revenue, slope
  +0.31, *t* = +9.92, +20.8 pp tercile spread). But the decisive autocorrelation-robust
  statistic is **NW *t* = +1.10** — below the desk's **t ≥ 2** bar — and the edge is entirely
  concentrated in the 2019-2021 boom (+245 bps/mo, dead at +17 bps since 2022). Literature
  (Rajgopal-Shevlin-Venkatachalam 2003) and the mechanism say the lead is real; **this thin
  post-ASC-606 tape cannot certify that the market underreacts to it.** WEAK, not REAL.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Net of 20 bps + borrow the point estimate barely moves
  (+87 bps/mo, Sharpe 0.49) — costs are *not* what kills it — but the net NW *t* is **+0.96**,
  statistically indistinguishable from zero, on a paper Sharpe that lives entirely in one
  bull regime. An uncertified, regime-concentrated paper edge is not a paycheck.
- **Does backlog lead sales? — CONFIRMED.** The accounting lead is real and large
  (*t* ≈ +9.9); the fundamental signal works. It is the *return* underreaction, not the
  fundamental, that this sample can't stand up.
